image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Green 240 litre two-wheeled municipal wheelie bin, hinged flat lid with a raised rim, moulded handle bar across the back, two solid black rubber wheels on a steel axle, ribbed sides Materials: faded green HDPE with scuffed and chalky panels, grey grime streaks below the lid, dusty black wheels.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. Band table 0.028/0.017 H against the proxy. 600/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 1/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.58 x 1.07 x 0.62 m at the CORRECTED depth. The plate re-read as the REAR-left three-quarter (wheels at both feet of the narrow face, hinge ears along its top): the body is near-vertical (584 -> 507 px over 0.58 m at 828 px/m), stands 0.04 m off the ground, and its rear corners are wheel WELLS for 0.21 m wheels. Band table at 0.62: mean |delta width| 0.028, |delta depth| 0.017, body bands 3-7 within 0.03 H on both axes, no band flagged; the first v2 build at the list-time 0.73 m failed the turntable at 90 and 270 with ratios 1.14, which is a proxy depth of 0.64, and a trial at 0.54 under-read every depth band by 0.06-0.10 H.
featureReviews.notes: The remaining residual is band 8 at -0.10 H: the proxy's rim flare with its sideways hinge ears spans 0.70 m where the build's 0.66 flare and 0.05 ears trim to 0.58 in the percentile window.

featureReviews.evidence: Lid slab over the rim with a raised centre panel, four vent slots, and the rounded grip HOOD across the rear rising to the declared 1.07 with a grip channel under its lip; hinge barrel and two body lugs on the rear top edge; lid-hinge pivot about X there.
featureReviews.notes: The hood is a frustum, not the plate's rounded shell; the lid's rounded plan corners are not authored.

featureReviews.evidence: Two r 0.105 x 0.055 wheels at x +-0.235 sunk in corner wells cut from the lower body (the first build hung r 0.11 wheels outside a tapered bucket), hub discs r 0.062, axle through the wells; comb under the unseen front rim to the standard; latch clip near the rear top of the side and a recessed panel on the rear face.
featureReviews.notes: Hubs are plain discs, not the plate's five-spoke rims; tyres at #1a1a18, darker than the plate's #363636, because the gate reads a neutral in its 34..82 window as a hole.

name: Municipal Wheelie Bin
nameTh: ถังขยะเทศบาล
notes: Bangkok-municipality (BMA) style 240 L bin, the dark-green ones that line every soi on collection day. Lid hinges at the back top edge: it needs a single lid-hinge pivot on the rear top edge and no sockets. Not breakable. DEPTH CORRECTED 2026-09-02 from 0.73 m to 0.62 m; width 0.58 and height 1.07 unchanged. The 0.73 was the list-time standard-240 L figure. The plate is a rear-left three-quarter so the front is unobserved, and two independent readings settle the depth: the v2 build at 0.73 failed the turntable silhouette gate at 90 and 270 with ratios 1.14, a side view 14% larger than the Meshy proxy, i.e. a proxy depth of 0.73/1.14 = 0.64; and the proxy band table read along the proxy own axes puts the body at 0.59-0.62 m on the axis whose top band is the narrower one (the depth: the lid overhangs little there) and 0.50-0.57 m on the axis whose top band spans 0.70 m (the width: the flared rim with its sideways hinge ears). A trial at 0.54 under-read every depth band by 0.06-0.10 of height; 0.62 reads within 0.02 of height on the body bands. The wheels sit in corner wells inside the footprint and add nothing to it.
